raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

`fused_recurrent_gated_delta_rule_packed_decode` is the GDN decode step of every linear-attention layer in Qwen3.5/Qwen3.8 hybrid models, and on SM90 it is the default path (Triton linear-attention backend, FP32 SSM state from the checkpoint's `mamba_ssm_dtype`). It launches `grid = (V / BV, B * HV)` with one warp per program and BV = 32, so at B = 1 with 48 value heads (Qwen3.8-27B at TP1) that is 192 single-warp programs on a 132-SM part, each walking a 128 x 32 state slice. On SM90 with an FP32 state, BV = 4 is faster at every measured shape.

This is the decode counterpart of the SM90 BV = 4 tile that `_select_recurrent_launch_config` already uses for GDN `target_verify`. Not a duplicate: #42372 also widens that branch to packed decode, but as part of a 753-line SSD weight-offload PR; this PR is only the tile change, with its own measurements. The same tile was merged in vLLM for the same kernel (vllm-project/vllm#63864).

## Modifications

`python/sglang/kernels/ops/attention/fla/fused_recurrent.py`: in `fused_recurrent_gated_delta_rule_packed_decode`, use BV = 4 when K = V = 128, the state is FP32 and `is_sm90_supported()`. Every other case keeps its current tile: BF16 states (no single tile wins everywhere on SM90), other architectures (including the existing SM100 B = 1 case), other head dims.

`test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_gdn_packed_decode_sm90_tile.py` (new, SM90 only): checks that an FP32 state launches with BV = 4 and gives bit-identical output and updated state to the BV = 32 launch (4 shapes, including a non-power-of-two batch), and that a BF16 state keeps BV = 32.

## Accuracy Tests

Each program reduces over the full K for its own V rows, so a narrower V tile computes the same recurrence in the same order. Output and updated state are bitwise identical to BV = 32 at all 110 FP32 points of the sweep below (and at all BF16 points, which keep BV = 32 anyway). Model outputs are therefore unchanged.

All numbers below are on main at eead03f (this PR's base) plus this change: the `lmsysorg/sglang:nightly-dev-cu13-20261028-586355a8` image (dependency pins identical to main's `pyproject.toml`; Triton 3.8.0, torch 2.14.1+cu130) with its `sglang` package replaced by the checkout. Tests on H200:

| test | result |
|---|---|
| `test_gdn_packed_decode_sm90_tile.py` (new) | 5 passed |
| `attention/unittests/gdn/test_linear_replayssm_decode.py` | 6 passed, 36 subtests passed |
| `attention/unittests/gdn/test_triton.py` | 13 passed, 26 subtests passed |
| `attention/test_gdn_noncontiguous_stride.py` | 8 passed |
| `attention/test_gdn_fused_split_head_ratios.py` | 4 passed |

## Speed Tests and Profiling

### Kernel (cold L2)

H200 NVL (132 SMs, 60 MiB L2), K = V = 128, BF16 qkv, QK L2-norm on, FP32 state. Each CUDA graph cycles through enough disjoint state slots that the state touched between two uses of a slot is >= 4x L2 (240 MiB), so the state is never L2-resident, as in a decode step. Kernel time from CUPTI (`torch.profiler`) over graph replays; 7 rounds with the tile order shuffled each round, median reported (round-to-round spread <= 1.7%). Speedup of BV = 4 over BV = 32:

| (H, HV) | B=1 | B=2 | B=4 | B=8 | B=16 | B=32 | B=64 | B=128 | B=256 | B=512 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| (16, 48) | 1.49x | 1.30x | 1.11x | 1.25x | 1.12x | 1.10x | 1.09x | 1.09x | 1.09x | 1.09x |
| (8, 24) | 1.75x | 1.50x | 1.30x | 1.10x | 1.25x | 1.12x | 1.11x | 1.10x | 1.09x | 1.10x |
| (4, 12) | 1.92x | 1.75x | 1.50x | 1.31x | 1.11x | 1.24x | 1.12x | 1.11x | 1.10x | 1.11x |
| (2, 6) | 1.98x | 1.94x | 1.76x | 1.50x | 1.31x | 1.11x | 1.23x | 1.11x | 1.10x | 1.10x |
| (16, 32) | 1.63x | 1.43x | 1.25x | 1.13x | 1.18x | 1.14x | 1.12x | 1.09x | 1.09x | 1.08x |
| (8, 16) | 1.84x | 1.65x | 1.42x | 1.25x | 1.12x | 1.18x | 1.14x | 1.11x | 1.09x | 1.08x |
| (4, 8) | 1.92x | 1.81x | 1.61x | 1.42x | 1.25x | 1.12x | 1.17x | 1.12x | 1.11x | 1.08x |
| (2, 4) | 1.93x | 1.88x | 1.79x | 1.58x | 1.40x | 1.25x | 1.12x | 1.16x | 1.11x | 1.11x |
| (16, 64) | 1.40x | 1.24x | 1.13x | 1.17x | 1.14x | 1.12x | 1.09x | 1.09x | 1.09x | 1.08x |
| (8, 32) | 1.61x | 1.41x | 1.25x | 1.13x | 1.19x | 1.15x | 1.12x | 1.10x | 1.08x | 1.08x |
| (4, 16) | 1.80x | 1.61x | 1.40x | 1.25x | 1.12x | 1.17x | 1.14x | 1.11x | 1.09x | 1.08x |

(16, 48), (8, 24), (4, 12), (2, 6) are Qwen3.8-27B at TP 1/2/4/8.

BV = 4 is the fastest of {4, 8, 16, 32} at all 110 points: 1.08-1.98x, geometric mean 1.26x. With a BF16 state the best tile varies (BV = 16 at 73 of 110 points, BV = 4 at 33, BV = 32 at 4; BV = 4 alone ranges 0.88-1.85x), so BF16 is left at 32.

Why (Nsight Compute, H200, Triton 3.8.0): with an FP32 state the BV = 32 kernel uses 212 registers per thread, so an SM holds at most 8 of these single-warp programs (12% theoretical occupancy); BV = 4 uses 56 registers and is limited only by the 32-blocks-per-SM cap (50%). At B = 1, (H, HV) = (16, 48), the 192 BV = 32 programs leave one or two warps per SM to cover DRAM latency (2.3% achieved occupancy, vs 16% with BV = 4). At B = 512 there is plenty of work, but DRAM throughput is still 81% of peak with BV = 32 vs 86% with BV = 4. DRAM traffic is the same for every tile (the repeated per-program q/k reads hit in L2), but a narrower tile executes more instructions: about 2x for BV = 4 vs BV = 32. With an FP32 state the kernel stays memory-bound and hides them. With a BF16 state the bytes halve, BV = 4 executes 2.4x the instructions of BV = 32 at B = 512 and reaches only 67% of DRAM peak, which is why BV = 4 is not used for BF16.

### End to end

Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 (48 GDN layers, FP32 SSM state from the checkpoint), main with and without this change (same image as above), one H200 NVL, TP1, default backends (Triton linear attention, FA3), `--disable-radix-cache --max-running-requests 64`. `sglang.bench_serving --dataset-name random-ids`, 1024 in / 128 out, range ratio 1, 4 warmup requests; 32 / 64 / 256 prompts at concurrency 1 / 8 / 32. Unpatched and patched servers interleaved (A B A B), 2 runs each, mean reported:

| concurrency | metric | unpatched | patched | change | predicted from kernel |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | median TPOT | 10.87 ms | 10.77 ms | -0.9% | -0.9% |
| 8 | median ITL | 11.90 ms | 11.62 ms | -2.3% | -1.5% |
| 32 | median ITL | 14.68 ms | 14.23 ms | -3.1% | -1.8% |
| 1 / 8 / 32 | output tok/s | 86.4 / 501.1 / 1067.3 | 87.5 / 509.5 / 1088.1 | +1.3 / +1.7 / +2.0% | |

All requests completed. At every concurrency both patched runs are faster than both unpatched runs (largest run-to-run spread 1.1%, at concurrency 8 unpatched). "Predicted" is the per-call kernel saving at that batch (H, HV = 16, 48) x 48 layers over the unpatched step time; the packed decode is 2.6% of a step at batch 1, 7.6% at batch 8 and 19% at batch 32. The measured gain at batch 8 and 32 is somewhat larger than this estimate. An earlier run of the same benchmark on `lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.22` (same `fused_recurrent.py`) gave -1.2% / -2.1% / -1.8%.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). (Not needed: no user-facing change.)
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

files.patch:
@@ -13,6 +13,10 @@
 from sglang.srt.utils import is_cuda
 
 
+def _is_sm90(device: torch.device) -> bool:
+    return torch.cuda.get_device_capability(device)[0] == 9
+
+
 @triton.jit(do_not_specialize=["T"])
 def fused_recurrent_gated_delta_rule_fwd_kernel(
     q,
@@ -373,6 +377,16 @@ def fused_recurrent_gated_delta_rule_packed_decode(
         and torch.cuda.get_device_capability(mixed_qkv.device)[0] == 10
     )
     BV = min(triton.next_power_of_2(V), 8 if use_small_value_tile else 32)
+    if (
+        is_cuda()
+        and K == V == 128
+        and initial_state.dtype == torch.float32
+        and _is_sm90(mixed_qkv.device)
+    ):
+        # Tuned on H200: with an FP32 state BV=4 is the fastest tile at every measured
+        # (H, HV, batch) and bit-identical to BV=32. No BF16-state tile wins everywhere
+        # on SM90, so BF16 keeps 32.
+        BV = 4
     num_stages = 3
     num_warps = 1

@@ -0,0 +1,89 @@
+"""SM90 packed GDN decode with an FP32 state uses BV=4, bit-identical to BV=32.
+
+``fused_recurrent_gated_delta_rule_packed_decode`` picks a narrower value tile on
+SM90 when the recurrent state is FP32. Each program still reduces over the full K
+for its own V rows, so the output and the updated state must match the default
+BV=32 launch bit for bit. BF16 states keep BV=32.
+"""
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from sglang.kernels.ops.attention.fla import fused_recurrent as fr
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cuda_ci
+
+register_cuda_ci(est_time=10, stage="base-b-kernel-unit", runner_config="1-gpu-large")
+
+pytestmark = pytest.mark.skipif(
+    not torch.cuda.is_available() or torch.cuda.get_device_capability()[0] != 9,
+    reason="SM90-only value-tile selection",
+)
+
+_K = _V = 128
+_KERNEL = fr.fused_recurrent_gated_delta_rule_packed_decode_kernel
+
+
+class _LaunchSpy:
+    """Records the BV of each packed-decode launch and forwards to the real kernel."""
+
+    def __init__(self, kernel):
+        self.kernel = kernel
+        self.bvs = []
+
+    def __getitem__(self, grid):
+        launch = self.kernel[grid]
+
+        def run(*args, **kwargs):
+            self.bvs.append(kwargs["BV"])
+            return launch(*args, **kwargs)
+
+        return run
+
+
+def _run(monkeypatch, case, state_dtype, sm90):
+    H, HV, B = case
+    gen = torch.Generator(device="cuda").manual_seed(H * 1000 + HV * 10 + B)
+
+    def randn(*shape):
+        return torch.randn(*shape, device="cuda", generator=gen)
+
+    mixed_qkv = randn(B, 2 * H * _K + HV * _V).to(torch.bfloat16)
+    a = randn(B, HV).to(torch.bfloat16)
+    b = randn(B, HV).to(torch.bfloat16)
+    A_log = randn(HV) * 0.1
+    dt_bias = randn(HV) * 0.1
+    # Slot 0 is the null slot; real sequences use slots 1..B.
+    state = (randn(B + 1, HV, _V, _K) * 0.02).to(state_dtype)
+    out = torch.empty(B, 1, HV, _V, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    indices = torch.arange(1, B + 1, device="cuda", dtype=torch.int32)
+
+    spy = _LaunchSpy(_KERNEL)
+    monkeypatch.setattr(
+        fr, "fused_recurrent_gated_delta_rule_packed_decode_kernel", spy
+    )
+    monkeypatch.setattr(fr, "_is_sm90", lambda device: sm90)
+    fr.fused_recurrent_gated_delta_rule_packed_decode(
+        mixed_qkv, a, b, A_log, dt_bias, _K**-0.5, state, out, indices, True
+    )
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+    return out, state, spy.bvs
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("case", [(16, 48, 1), (16, 48, 64), (2, 6, 1), (4, 16, 257)])
+def test_fp32_state_uses_bv4_and_matches_bv32(monkeypatch, case):
+    out, state, bvs = _run(monkeypatch, case, torch.float32, sm90=True)
+    ref_out, ref_state, ref_bvs = _run(monkeypatch, case, torch.float32, sm90=False)
+    assert bvs == [4] and ref_bvs == [32]
+    assert torch.equal(out, ref_out)
+    assert torch.equal(state, ref_state)
+
+
+def test_bf16_state_keeps_bv32(monkeypatch):
+    _, _, bvs = _run(monkeypatch, (16, 48, 8), torch.bfloat16, sm90=True)
+    assert bvs == [32]
